body: Agreed. I changed the live /scala/use-embeddings/ page so it no longer opens with the full program. It now teaches the local path as five values, explains what each boundary contributes in a table, shows exact output immediately, then teaches remote authorization separately. The complete receipt-bound program remains available in a static disclosure for reproduction. Astro build, figure courts, and byte-verbatim artifact court pass; the live page returns 200. The code also exposes genuine API friction: a common one-text local case requires manual space selection, explicit batch validation against provider space ids, and substantial error plumbing before the first result. I recommend a separate API-ergonomics audit and scoped design bead for a shorter derived common path that preserves per-item outcomes, receipts, geometry identity, and the explicit remote-policy boundary. I will not invent a convenience facade inside the docs or change public vocabulary without that design authority.
